entries.claim: The elision mark records `serde_json::to_vec(value).len()`, i.e. the canonical reserialization of the parsed subtree, not the bytes actually removed from the archived JSONL line. That makes `verbatimElided` lie whenever the source subtree used escape sequences, different number spellings, or any other non-canonical JSON encoding.
entries.failure_scenario: A `toolUseResult` containing a string like `"\u0041"` is stored as if only 3 bytes were removed because the parsed value reserializes to `"A"`; the source line actually shed many more bytes, so the accounting disagrees with the archive delta and any later audit that trusts the mark gets the wrong size.

counter_evidence.note: The mechanism is stated correctly and the divergence is real, but the consequence the scenario rests on does not exist. Nothing in production reads the mark: grep for elided_bytes and ELISION_MARK across crates/ finds capture.rs itself and crates/verbatim-core/tests/capture.rs and nowhere else, so there is no accounting, no archive-delta comparison and no audit for the figure to disagree with - it is documentary. The measurement basis is also chosen rather than accidental: the Lean arm two lines above says so in as many words, measured on the compact serialization, which is what a transcript writes, and it is the same serialized value the threshold compares. Reaching the divergence needs a source line that is not compact JSON, which the Claude Code writer does not emit. Downgraded from medium to low and queued as an open item: the honest fix is to say in the doc comment that the figure is the canonical size of what was dropped, not the source bytes.

entries.claim: `CaptureMode::Minimal` elides unconditionally, even when the replacement mark is larger than the subtree it replaces. That means the "minimal" mode can grow some records instead of shrinking them.
entries.failure_scenario: A tiny `toolUseResult` or `attachment` such as `{"stdout":"ok"}` is replaced by `{"verbatimElided":...}`; for small enough payloads the replacement is larger than the original, so a "minimal" ingest can store more bytes than `full` for that record and break the intended size-reduction guarantee.

counter_evidence.note: The scenario asserts a guarantee the mode does not make. Minimal is the mode that drops the large bodies unconditionally - the choice of how much of each record to keep, not a per-record size bound - and the measured effect on the plan fixture is 28,785 bytes at full against 2,436 at minimal (reports/plan-5.md, task 3). The growth case is bounded at the mark object itself, about twenty bytes, and only for a payload smaller than that; it does not compound, because elide_fields skips a value is_mark already accepts (capture.rs:137-140), so a second pass over an elided record rewrites nothing. There is no state in which minimal stores more than full for a transcript, and no code that depends on per-record shrinkage.
